anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 profile has a 5x5x3 isometric pile with four directly exposed diamonds, one lava hazard and one fragile support; the visible task is camera rotation plus depth-sorted click-ray extraction. Anthill d1 removes hidden scouting and excavation, but still requires a resource/production phase, a live one-wave intercept decision, and a later assault. It is therefore above this low static/spatial anchor in dependent state and temporal control, while the comparison does not claim that its mouse precision is harder than the voxel raycast.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 full profile is one 680x410 active-cursor search with 26 noise stars, two false convergence points and one accepted click; moving the cursor supplies local visual feedback and the grader checks the final point. anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 full profile continuously drags an analog tilt knob through three ordered lamps, three walls and three wells under momentum/friction before settling in a cup. Anthill d3 has less continuous motor control and only one branch choice, but replaces that with persistent scouting/digging/economy state, a moving formation whose direction must be inferred from recent screenshots, irreversible interception timing and a survivor-dependent assault. These are comparable L3-scale demands on different control axes, rather than evidence that Anthill d3 should jump to L4.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 full profile routes a sealed die through five face gates in an 18x11 warehouse using 48-105 rolls and only sparse orientation scanners; every accepted roll changes position and orientation, so earlier actions constrain later gate choices. Anthill d4 instead has two sequential moving contacts and survivor-dependent soldier redirection, but only two binary lane decisions and no long hidden orientation route. It is a nearby high comparison; the one-wave current d3 is below this L4 profile.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 simplified profile requires four changing-board swaps, an exact score, at least seven cascade waves and a forbidden candy; each accepted swap changes the board and refill stream that determine the next decision. Anthill d5 has a genuine concurrent dependency—two overlapping response windows require disjoint live soldier groups before either impact—but only two waves with deterministic timing and no combinatorial board route. Thus d5 is a high profile approaching the L5 anchor, while current d3 is clearly below it; repetition and clock length are not credited by themselves.

visible_baseline_solution: At d3/full, a screenshot-only agent sees the match clock, seeds, worker count, soldiers plus production queue, brood state, own queen and a hidden rival-queen value before contact. The map shows the home queen, brood, seed pile, listening front, two labelled tunnels, visible workers and a minimap; after scouting it shows the rival, outpost build progress, the moving four-ant formation, the marked intercept line and sidebar statuses such as CONTACT IN BAND and VECTOR MOVING. Select exactly two workers on the map, press D and click the visible brood marker; select one worker, press S and click the listening front, then leave that worker assigned for 40 ticks; select the remaining workers, press G and click the seed pile. Watch the brood percentage and seed/queue HUD, issue R when two seeds are available until enough soldiers exist, and use several recent screenshots while the formation crosses its response band to determine whether its vertical motion is NORTH or SOUTH. Press M and click the corresponding tunnel before the band closes. After the raid resolves, select the surviving soldiers, press M and click the revealed rival queen, wait for VICTORY, and certify. The full path requires map selection or marquee selection, minimap/arrow panning when a destination is off-screen, an 8-pixel tunnel hit band and correctly timed two-stage command gestures. A wrong committed lane cannot be retried for that wave; a late or pre-band march is rejected, and the rival assault is rejected until every raid is cleared. The verifier then replays the command ledger and requires a terminal won state, own queen above zero, rival queen at zero and every wave successfully intercepted.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The source supports a strict relative progression without treating the current label as authoritative: d1 has one visible seeded contact and no setup dependency; d2 adds hidden scouting and exact one-worker excavation; d3 increases the excavation/work and raid burden but still has one defense window; d4 adds a sequential second wave whose losses change the next allocation; d5 overlaps the windows and requires disjoint groups before either impact. The current d3/full task is above the approved L1/L2 examples, comparable to the approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board despite trading continuous motor control for multi-agent state planning, and below the longer hidden-orientation L4 and changing-board L5 examples. Keeping d3 is therefore better supported than relabelling it from source alone.

concise_summary: Keep Anthill Front at its implemented d3/full baseline. Source inspection supports five distinct ordered profiles: setup dependencies at d2-d3, sequential survivor-dependent defense at d4, and overlapping disjoint allocation at d5. The baseline is comparable to the approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board, above the L1/L2 anchors and below the approved L4/L5 high-dependency examples; absolute calibration remains pending.
